answer: A network of AI agents resists Sybil attacks by anchoring each identity to verifiable computation. Every agent must solve a unique proof-of-work puzzle that pins its key to a specific vertex of the network identity graph, making mass fake accounts prohibitively expensive. Agents then cross-attest each other's honest output, building a public atlas of accumulated work that newcomers consult for reputation. Peers that refuse real work lose their neighbors' attestations, which act as a lantern exposing sockpuppets to the whole economy. Flooding the system thus costs more than it can ever return.
